declared_record.derivation: REPORTED numeric coefficient with ASSUMED transport. See declared scientific assumptions; this parameter is not an inferred target estimate.

relevant_assumptions.description: Equal-weight virtual rows are posited draws from the requested labweight-weighted selected complete-case distribution. Target age/sex/BMI frequencies and their dependence are unidentified. Declining decade frequencies and modest female excess are author assumptions; they are not PNS estimates.

BMI is a right-skewed shifted gamma conditional on age/sex, with modest rise through middle age then decline. All numerical distribution settings are assumed; no source BMI marginal is relabelled as a target estimate.

The BP mean surfaces are assumed: rising SBP, DBP rising until55 then declining, lower female conditional means with an age-varying SBP contrast. Beijing older-group means motivate the scale only and do not identify adjusted age/sex functions or target intercepts.

INTERSALT pooled BMI coefficients are used as the conditional slopes per1 BMI unit. This explicitly assumes their richer adjustment, centre pooling, treatment composition, age20-59 range, device, era and country differences can be transported to all target ages. It does not identify a causal effect; task OLS slopes can also differ due to nonlinear age/sex terms and truncation.

A heteroscedastic bivariate Gaussian conditional residual is assumed. SBP SD rises with age and DBP SD rises slightly; rho=0.50 is an assumed residual correlation. It is not the Beijing raw r=0.5451 relabelled: age/sex/BMI covariance explained by the mean surface remains unidentified. Beijing marginal SDs/raw covariance only motivate orders of magnitude.

Residual variation combines biological variation, unmodelled treatment/selection and measurement error. No separate treatment mixture is identified. INTERSALT uses two random-zero readings, Beijing two Omron readings, target three G-TECH MA100 readings with unknown released final algorithm. Zero additional device/averaging offset is assumed, not measured. Baseline interview BP/BMI are modeled; later lab-visit timing is not substituted.

BMI is rejected only if it exceeds the envelope 200/(1.2^2); its shifted-gamma lower endpoint12 is assumed and inside dictionary feasibility. BP residual pairs are redrawn conditional on fixed covariates until SBP60-290, DBP30-200 and SBP>DBP. This is an explicit conditional truncation assumption for eligible physiological records, not automatic clipping; it can change moments/slopes. Weight and height themselves are not reconstructed.

reasons: SBP age-by-sex interaction; DBP age hinge at55; nonlinear conditional BMI mean.
Residual scales depend on age; pooled residual correlation need not equal fixed-covariate rho.
BP pairs redrawn conditional on fixed age/sex/BMI; BMI redrawn conditional on fixed age/sex.
Generated finite-sample regression/correlation also varies over Monte Carlo draws.

model_implied_requested_value.reason: No exact population projection or exact post-selection residual-correlation calculation is present or proven in this audit. Literal coefficients/rho and finite generated estimates are not substituted. The generator was neither imported nor executed.

relevant_assumptions.description: Assumed target analytical law: completed age=floor(20+60*Beta(1.4,1.8)); female probability0.53+0.001*(age-45). No target empirical demographics support these numbers. Rows are equal-weight draws from the hypothesized labweight-weighted selected distribution; no claim of national representation.

Assumed BMI conditional mean=26+0.07*(min(age,60)-45)-0.08*max(age-60,0)+0.8*female. BMI=14+lognormal with logSD0.34, centered to that mean. These age/sex dependencies, skew and scale are assumptions, not recovered source moments.

Assumed mean SBP=125+0.55*(age-50)+0.15*max(age-55,0)+female*(-5+0.08*(age-50))+0.7754*(BMI-25). Assumed mean DBP=78.5+0.22*(age-50)-0.50*max(age-55,0)-2*female+0.5967*(BMI-25). Beijing age contrasts motivate allowing different late-age trends but do not numerically identify these coefficients. Treatment/disease are marginalized into this descriptive law, never excluded.

The two reported INTERSALT BMI coefficients are provisionally used as additive conditional slopes in the wider target age range. This assumes source adjustment beyond age/sex does not change the intended transported BMI relationship, and stable associations across country/era/selection/device/treatment. It is not causal identification. Nonlinear age patterns, selection rejection and random variation can make the requested linear-regression projection differ.

Assumed standardized bivariate Student-t residuals with8 degrees of freedom and common mixing draw; SBP scale=14.5+0.10*max(age-50,0), DBP scale9.5, correlation0.65. Before feasibility conditioning these are conditional SDs/correlation, not source-reported quantities. Choosing a positively correlated finite-variance law recognizes shared BP variability without relabelling Beijing raw correlation as residual correlation. Tail shape, heteroskedasticity, correlation and scales are uncalibrated assumptions.

The covariate distribution is specified directly for the analytical complete-case population. Rejection retains BP within source-dictionary SBP60-290 and DBP30-200, with assumed physiological ordering SBP>DBP. BMI is required only to lie within the existential range30/(2.1^2) through200/(1.2^2) implied by the weight/height dictionary. No clipping occurs. Without generated height, weight, pregnancy or response processes, this does not reconstruct their joint selection; their marginal impact is assumed absorbed into the selected law.

Transport source measurements to final baseline PNS BP through an identity-unit, zero additional mean-shift assumption. Source two-reading manual INTERSALT and automated Beijing protocols differ from target three automated G-TECH readings after seated rest and unknown final aggregation. Differences in noise, device, repeated visits and timing remain inside assumed residual law. Source coefficients/SDs cannot quantify that transport uncertainty.

relevant_assumptions.description: Assumed selected analytical covariate law: age=20+59*Beta(1.45,1.8); female probability=.53+.001*(age-50). relevant_assumptions.description: ASSUMED target covariate law: age is20+59*Beta(1.35,1.75); female probability logistic(0.16+0.06*(age-50)/10). No target demographic values supplied or inferred. Dependence is explicitly weakly age-varying, not inferred independence.

ASSUMED conditional BMI: lognormal with log median log(26.5)+0.02*a-0.012*a^2+0.025*female, a=(age-50)/10, log SD0.18; rejection outside12-65kg/m2. All BMI location, spread, age and sex dependencies are assumptions, not recovered target statistics.

ASSUMED joint conditional BP location: SBP126+5.5*a+1.0*a^2-4*female+0.7754*(BMI-25); DBP79+1.8*a-0.7*a^2-2.5*female+0.5967*(BMI-25). Nonlinear age patterns permit later-life divergence; numeric age/sex/intercept parameters are not source-adjusted effects. Source age-group contrasts are descriptive context only.

Reported INTERSALT per-kg/m2 slopes are used as conditional BMI coefficients, assuming transport from1980s multi-country ages20-59, richer sodium/potassium/alcohol adjustment and inverse-variance pooling to this2013 selected Brazilian age20-79 analytical distribution. No age/BMI interaction is assumed. Treatment and omitted-variable differences can invalidate this. The requested linear age-adjusted regression need not equal these conditional coefficients because age is nonlinear and joint rejection can shift moments.

ASSUMED conditional Gaussian BP disturbances: SD_SBP=13+0.08*(age-20), SD_DBP=10.5mmHg, conditional rho=0.55. Rho is an explicitly assumed residual parameter, not the derived Beijing raw r. Beijing raw moments offer broad context only; conditional dependence is unidentified. Heteroscedasticity and nonlinear-age residuals imply the requested OLS residual r need not equal0.55.

ASSUMED joint support: BMI12-65; BP proposals are rejected jointly until60<=SBP<=290,30<=DBP<=200 and SBP>DBP. BP validity bounds represent analytical selection; positive PP is an additional feasibility assumption. Conditional redraw keeps covariates fixed, assuming their law already represents the selected population. No clipping or boundary mass; this changes the pre-selection Gaussian law and can alter slopes. Weight/height are not output and their separate selection effects are absorbed into the assumed BMI law; the BMI interval is compatible with at least one valid height/weight pair but not a reconstruction of their distribution.

Source-to-target transport assumes measured BMI and final seated BP have comparable units, but does not assert device equivalence. Target uses three G-TECH MA100 readings two minutes apart after>=5min rest, usually leftarm; released final averaging rule is unknown. INTERSALT averages two random-zero readings, Beijing two Omron readings; no separately estimated measurement correction is available. Residual scales integrate biological and protocol variation. BP/anthropometry remain baseline, not later lab-visit outcomes.

Target excludes reported pregnancy only and includes treatment, diabetes and hypertension. Those features are marginalized rather than explicitly generated. Source selection and treatment prevalence differ; pregnancy exclusion, lab participation and labweight effects are unknown transport assumptions. No causal or individual-recovery claim.

reasons: Quadratic age terms in both BP means and conditional log-BMI median; age-varying sex probability.

BP pairs redrawn conditional on fixed age/sex/BMI; BMI redrawn conditional on fixed age/sex within assumed12–65 interval.
Generated finite-sample regression/correlation also varies over Monte Carlo draws.

Source/request adjustment and weighting differ; generated projection also depends on nonlinear means, covariate laws, heteroscedasticity, truncation/selection, finite draws, source estimation and reference uncertainty. Five authors share one packet, the identical two copied slopes, a host/workflow and a real reference. Narrow author variation can coexist with a shared discrepancy; its SD is not calibrated uncertainty.
